name: Salt Basin release loop
summary: Every code change moves build → initial check → integrate → browser validation → triage → fix → re-validate, looping until every training journey passes or a failure needs a business definition. Every step leaves a dated log traced to the version before it.

roles.name: Build agent
roles.does: Builds one feature on its own branch from the current integration head, runs the initial check, and writes the design/change spec and the training spec.

roles.name: Integration agent
roles.does: Merges a build or fix branch into the integration branch one at a time, resolves conflicts without losing either side's behaviour, re-runs the build, and commits pending logs.

roles.name: Validation agent
roles.does: Follows a training spec literally in a real browser against a freshly seeded database and records pass/fail per step with evidence. Never substitutes script checks for the journey.

roles.name: Triage agent
roles.does: Turns failed steps into triage items: reproduces each, finds the root cause, classifies it (defect, spec error, environment, needs business definition), and dedupes against earlier rounds.

roles.name: Fix agent
roles.does: Fixes the root cause of fixable triage items on its own branch, re-runs the failed journey steps itself, and writes fix notes the validator receives.
produces: fix notes appended to the change spec

roles.name: Release recorder
roles.does: Writes the release log: every feature, round, failure, fix and final result, plus anything escalated for a business definition.

roles.name: Amendment reviewer
roles.does: Decides proposed spec amendments against specGovernance.reviewChecklist; for approved ones edits the training spec and freezes the next baseline version on its own branch; sends removals and weakened expectations to the owner. Never the agent that proposed the change.

stages.note: Only when a round produced spec_error / coverage_gap items, AMBIGUOUS steps or fixer-proposed steps. Approved amendments are integrated before the next validation round, which then runs on the new baseline version.
Listed for the owner to define; never guessed.

initialCheck: server boots against a fresh database
the feature's own journeys pass when the builder walks them once
when tools/release-tracker/ changed: node tools/release-tracker/sync-setup-guide.mjs exits 0 (embedded page copy matches index.html)
gates.validation: Every step of every journey in the feature's training spec passes in a real browser twice — point-and-click on desktop and as a full walkthrough at 390px — with no page errors and no failed network requests the spec does not expect, and every capability is also reachable through the API and an MCP tool (see interfaceParity).
gates.noSilentCaps: When a feature reaches maxFixRounds still failing, it is recorded as not passed with its open triage items — never reported as done.
gates.push: The integration branch is pushed only when the release log shows every feature passed, or the owner says otherwise.
gates.baseline: Before validation round 1 a frozen baseline exists for the feature, and release-spec-baseline.mjs check passes on every merge (specGovernance).

triageClasses.note: The training spec, not the product, is wrong. Never edited by a fix agent: triage writes the proposed wording as a spec amendment, the amendment reviewer decides it against specGovernance.reviewChecklist, and only an approved amendment changes the spec (new baseline version).
Test setup problem; fixed in the harness and noted, never hidden.
Escalated to the owner with the exact question.

Something the change spec requires that no baseline step tests (found by a validator observation or a reconciliation requirement gap). Becomes a proposed added step in a spec amendment; it does not change the current round score.

changeSpec: Traces to: prior spec versions and commits this builds on or supersedes
What changed, data model (additive only), server, client
Fix notes per round (appended by fix agents)
trainingSpec: Where things are (reachable from the UI — no API-only configuration)
Numbered journeys: action → exact expected result
testResult: Per journey step: pass/fail, what was seen, screenshot path
Fix details received (rounds after the first)

privacy: This repository is public: logs and specs use fictional data only and never name an employer or application target.

sessionMapping.when: End of every session (Claude Code or in-app agent run)
sessionMapping.does: Analyse the session: what was learned or repeated, and where each piece belongs so the next session doesn't re-derive it

destinations.context: CLAUDE.md / skill reference docs — stable facts every session needs
destinations.prompt: skills, saved workflows, agent role prompts — repeatable procedures
destinations.cache: stable prompt prefixes and reusable reference blocks kept unchanged so they stay cached
destinations.memory: the agent memory register (docs/active-universal-salt-basin-agent-memory-register.md) — decisions, preferences, open questions

metrics: input, cache-write, cache-read and output tokens
estimated spend (price table editable in the UI)
sessionMapping.privacy: Only metrics and the mapping summary are committed; never transcript text or personal data.

bugEscalation.rule: A bug is the same bug when triage links it to an earlier item (same root cause or same failing step after a fix). Once a bug has had maxFixAttemptsPerBug fix attempts and validation still fails it, it leaves the automated loop with status needs_human: its full history (each triage, fix and re-test) goes to the owner and no agent touches it until a person decides.

tracker: Every agent start/finish, bug and status change is shown live in the release tracker (the tracker artifact in the Claude Code session, synced from the workflow journal by scripts/release-tracker-sync.mjs; there is no platform screen).

failureReconciliation.rule: An agent finishing is not the work finishing. Every failure, refusal, partial step, known limitation or deviation an agent reports is reconciled by a separate agent that verifies it on the branch and classifies it (product_defect, requirement_gap, owner_direction_conflict, test_harness, environment, process, informational) as resolved — only with evidence — or unresolved. Unresolved items are carried into the fix loop as bugs; a feature cannot pass while any remain.

liveLogging: Validators append each checked expectation and every page error or failed request to /var/tmp/.../<feature>/round-N/steps.jsonl as it happens; the tracker shows them live, so a failure is visible before the round ends.

scopeCheck.rule: After triage and before fixing, a scope agent decides whose bug each item is: this_feature (the feature's diff or spec caused it — it blocks the feature), pre_existing (it reproduces on the base before this feature's commits — backlog, non-blocking), other_feature (another feature's change caused it — reassigned to that feature as owner, non-blocking here), or process_note (a test-harness, environment or spec-wording problem, not a product bug — recorded, non-blocking). Each decision carries evidence (a base-branch reproduction, the commit that introduced it, or the file it lives in). A feature whose only remaining items are out of scope ends as passed_with_backlog; the backlog stays on the tracker and is never deleted. Exception (2026-10-10): an item that makes a frozen step of THIS feature fail stays this feature’s to fix whatever its scope (older code or another feature’s file); a feature never ends passed or passed_with_backlog while a baseline step fails. Bug ids are qualified with the feature key (<feature>-<id>).

interfaceParity.rule: Every capability a training spec exercises must be usable through all three interfaces: (1) the website — point-and-click from the World Shell on desktop AND a full walkthrough at 390px phone width, with no typed URLs, API calls, scripts or database edits standing in for any step or precondition (test accounts from scripts/create-test-member.mjs are the only setup exception); (2) the API — the same route the UI uses, with the same permission checks; (3) MCP — a tool in the platform MCP server (server/lib/mcpToolRegistry.js) that calls the same server function, with the same permission checks. A step that can only be done through an API, script or typed URL fails as a UI gap. A capability with no MCP tool fails as an MCP gap once the platform MCP server exists; before that, it is recorded and assigned to the platform-mcp feature.
interfaceParity.added: 2026-10-09 (owner: 'if the agent user testing a feature cannot test the training guides with a point and click or mobile walk through then it's going to fail')

specGovernance.rule: Each round tests the same frozen set of steps against the code under test. Only the code varies between retries; the steps, fixtures, accounts and environment are fixed constraints. A training spec is frozen as a versioned baseline (docs/training/baselines/<feature>/v<N>.json) before its first validation round. Every step carries a stable id written into the spec ([J3.2], [E.1], [P.1]); an id is never renumbered or reused. Validators, triage and fix agents never edit training specs or baselines. Any added, changed or removed step, precondition or fixture is a spec amendment (docs/spec-amendments/<feature>/A<n>.json) proposed with its reason and decided by a separate amendment reviewer against a fixed checklist; only an approved amendment changes the spec and freezes the next baseline version. The integrator refuses a merge whose spec differs from its latest baseline or whose baseline lacks an approved amendment.

stepIds.precondition: P.<n> (setup: a failed precondition blocks the steps after it; it is not scored)
stepIds.newSteps: get the next unused number in their group, so earlier ids keep their meaning across versions
stepIds.retired: listed in the baseline and never reused

specGovernance.scoring: Score = steps passed / scored steps in the pinned baseline. A step passes only when every required surface (desktop and mobile for browser steps, cli for command steps, fixed in the baseline) passed. A step with no result is not_run and counts as not passed. Results for ids outside the baseline are observations: they go to triage as possible coverage gaps and never change the score.
specGovernance.comparability: Scores are compared like for like only within one baseline version. When an approved amendment moves a feature to a new version, the next report and the tracker show the baseline version beside the score and the diff (same / changed / added / retired ids), never a bare change in the step count.

proposedBy: fix agent (steps proving a requirement gap it built)
amendment.decidedBy: amendment reviewer agent, never the proposer; the owner for anything the checklist sends to a person
fields: changes[{op: add|change|retire, stepId, before, after, tracesTo, whyNeeded}]
review{status: proposed|approved|rejected|needs_owner, reviewer, checklist, note, at}

reviewChecklist: Traced: every added or changed step names the change-spec requirement or owner direction it proves (tracesTo).
Not weaker: a changed expected result is at least as strict as before, unless the evidence shows the old expectation contradicts the change spec or owner direction (then say which).
Retire only duplicates: removing a step is approved only when another step tests the same thing (name it); any other removal is needs_owner.
Exact: action plus exact expected result (labels, text, values, counts); no 'should look right', no 'roughly'.
Reachable: the step is walkable by point-and-click on desktop and at 390px (interfaceParity), or is a cli step by design.
Deterministic: same result every run against the fixed constraints (no dependence on wall-clock time, random data, earlier failed steps, or leftovers from another test); timing tolerances are stated.
Fictional data only; fixtures written in the spec, never fetched.
Independent of the fix: the step tests behaviour, not the implementation the fixer chose.

Errors are plain and coloured by severity: any step that checks an error or warning requires the message to state the actual problem in plain words a member understands (no developer terms such as JSON, 500, null as the main message; technical detail may follow on its own line), and the colour that fits: red for a failure or a rejected input, amber only for a caution where nothing failed (owner direction 2026-10-10).

testConstraints.database: fresh database per validator, booted once, then npm run seed; nothing else pre-loaded
testConstraints.accounts: scripts/create-test-member.mjs: member@test.local and the admin, platform and career terms accepted (--no-terms only for steps that test terms)
testConstraints.browser: the pinned Chromium named in the release-loop args; no other browser
testConstraints.fixtures: only the fixtures written in the spec and its appendices, created through the UI unless a precondition says otherwise
testConstraints.codeUnderTest: the integration-branch commit named in the report; the only variable between rounds

specGovernance.added: 2026-10-09 (owner: 'some of the fails that were re validated have different test steps in the retries; new test steps need to also be thought through, there needs to be more of a confined release governance so that the variables can test against a set of fixed constraints')
